events.title: A rover mission reaches Mars
events.description: Pathfinder lands carrying the small Sojourner rover.

events.title: A major investment fund needs rescue
events.description: Banks and securities firms invest in Long-Term Capital Management after heavy losses threaten its survival.

events.title: The euro begins
events.description: Eleven countries start sharing a currency for financial transactions. Euro notes and coins will arrive later.

what_happened_next.text:
Intel finished this window at nearly ten times its starting value, Microsoft at about six times and Disney at a little over twice its start. The broad U.S. and international share baskets also gained. That was a strong five years for these choices, but it was not a smooth line and the result could not be read from the August 1995 starting page.

The companies were making different moves. Microsoft reported fiscal-1998 revenue of $14.48 billion, up 28%, as Windows 98 upgrade sales passed one million. Disney opened Animal Kingdom in 1998, adding a fourth park to Walt Disney World. Intel introduced Pentium III chips in 1999 for newer internet and media uses. These milestones describe business activity; they do not prove what caused each share’s exact return.

The same years brought Pathfinder’s Mars landing, a rescue of a heavily indebted investment fund, and the euro’s start for financial transactions. Good and worrying news arrived together. A company share that finished far above its start could still have fallen along the way. A broad basket combined many businesses, lowering dependence on one product or management team without guaranteeing a gain.

reflection.what_people_were_focused_on: Windows 95, Netscape’s stock-market debut and Disney’s expansion made technology and entertainment exciting news.
reflection.what_actually_mattered: The chosen chip and software shares gained much more than the broad basket in this window. They still had difficult months, and their results do not describe every technology company.
reflection.what_faded_away: The launch-day buzz did not tell you the size of five-year gains. New leadership and big deals were plans whose results still had to unfold.
reflection.what_nobody_knew: Nobody knew the exact path or the final ranking. Stopping the chart in August 2000 leaves later events outside the result.

hot:1995-08:microsoft.text: Microsoft reported record fiscal 1998 revenue of $14.48 billion in July 1998, up 28% from a year earlier. It also said more than one million Windows 98 upgrade licenses had sold within weeks of the June release, showing customers were paying to update software on existing PCs.

hot:1995-08:disney.text: Disney opened Animal Kingdom at Walt Disney World on April 22, 1998, adding the resort’s fourth theme park. Families could spend more time on rides and shows and needed food and hotel services, giving Disney new ways to earn visitor spending.

hot:1995-08:intel.text: Intel introduced the Pentium III processor on February 26, 1999, for PCs with richer internet, video and 3-D uses. The chip gave computer makers another option for newer, more powerful machines as the PC market kept expanding.
